messages.author: efd244536ec2792f
messages.subject: Multisite model with m-array
parts:
Hello all, 
I'm trying to run a multisite model based on data from an m-array.
I have 5 sites and the tricky thing about this model is that I have my data in quarterly format (4 quarters over ~22 years = 88 occasions to be precise). I want to estimate the posteriors on an annual or seasonal basis (i.e. summarise the information either by year so as to have only 22 posteriors, or by season so as to have only 4 parameters (quarter 1, 2, 3, 4)). I hope I haven't lost you so far.
The good news is that I've managed to run these models in the simple case (without multi-states) and also in the multi-state case (where I had individuals not according to sites but according to their stage of development, but I only have 3 stages and not 5 like the sites).
In this model, it doesn't run and I have the impression that this is because of the Dirichlet function (in fact if you replace 
    psi1[1:5] ~ ddirch(alpha[1:5])
    psi2[1:5] ~ ddirch(alpha[1:5])
    psi3[1:5] ~ ddirch(alpha[1:5])
    psi4[1:5] ~ ddirch(alpha[1:5])
    psi5[1:5] ~ ddirch(alpha[1:5])
by 
    psi1[1:5] <- rep(1/5, 5)
    psi2[1:5 ] <- rep(1/5, 5)
    psi3[1:5] <- rep(1/5, 5)
    # psi4[1:5] <- rep(1/5, 5)
    # psi5[1:5] <- rep(1/5, 5), 
the model runs without a problem). I can't understand why my model is stuck at: "Defining model
Building model Setting data and initial values Running calculate on model [Note] Any error reports that follow may simply reflect missing values in model variables. Checking model sizes and dimensions [Note] This model is not fully initialized. This is not an error. To see which variables are not initialized, use model$initializeInfo(). For more information on model initialization, see help(modelInitialization).
Checking model calculations".
Thank you very much for your help,
Have a nice day,
Amélie

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Multisite model with m-array
parts:
Hi Amélie,

I'm not seeing that the model gets stuck. Instead I see an error occurring when the MCMC is configured that cause MCMC configuration to fail. We've tracked that down to a bug in how nimble checks conjugacy with the complicated structure of how you define `pr`.

We'll fix that in the next release, but for now, please turn off conjugacy checking before running `nimbleMCMC`.

You can do this by setting a nimble option:

nimbleOptions(MCMCuseConjugacy = FALSE)

This shouldn't affect how sampling is done, because conjugate samplers wouldn't be assigned to your model in any case.

If that doesn't address things, let us know. (In particular, it may be that the 'getting stuck' problem is a distinct problem.)

-chris

messages.author: efd244536ec2792f
messages.subject: Re: Multisite model with m-array
parts:
Hi Chris, 
Thank you so much for your help.

Since I couldn't find a solution using the dirichlet distribution in the model (probably due to the configuration of the MCMCs as you've just explained, but to be honest I wouldn't have been able to find this issue). 
I coded myself to obtain dirichlet distributions using gamma distributions:

    for(i in 1:ns){
      lpsi1[i] ~ dgamma(1,1)
      lpsi2[i] ~ dgamma(1,1)
      lpsi3[i] ~ dgamma(1,1)
      lpsi4[i] ~ dgamma(1,1)
      lpsi5[i] ~ dgamma(1,1)
    }
    psi1[1:ns] <- lpsi1[1:ns]/sum(lpsi1[1:ns])
    psi2[1:ns] <- lpsi2[1:ns]/sum(lpsi2[1:ns])
    psi3[1:ns] <- lpsi3[1:ns]/sum(lpsi3[1:ns])
    psi4[1:ns] <- lpsi4[1:ns]/sum(lpsi4[1:ns])
    psi5[1:ns] <- lpsi5[1:ns]/sum(lpsi5[1:ns])

With this method, the models run smoothly.
Does this sound right to you?
That way seems correct for you also?
Thanks again for your time and solution !
Amélie

But I don't know which approach (using gammas or using Dirichlet) will give better MCMC mixing.
